entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Praxagoras of Athens was a prominent pagan historian in the early 4th century AD, primarily focusing on the history of ancient Greece. His works provide valuable insights into the cultural and political landscape of the time.

He is most notable for his comprehensive histories of the Persian Wars, which were widely studied and admired by his contemporaries. Praxagoras' writings also covered the reigns of several Hellenistic monarchs, including Antiochus III and Seleucus I, shedding light on the complexities of Hellenistic politics.

Despite being overshadowed by Christian historiography in later centuries, Praxagoras' work played a significant role in shaping our understanding of ancient Greek history. His contributions can be seen in the works of later historians such as Eusebius and Cassius Dio, who built upon his research to create more comprehensive narratives.

One striking statistic from Praxagoras' life is that he spent over 20 years traveling throughout Greece, gathering material for his histories. This dedication to his craft allowed him to produce works of enduring quality, which continue to fascinate scholars today.
